dimension_justifications.contribution: The contribution is a useful integration of ownership, lifecycle, execution, fault, and accounting receipts into an executable audit for hybrid KV/recurrent state. The novelty claim is carefully narrowed and credibly positioned against paged/prefix caching, hybrid-cache management, and testing precedents (Section 2; Tables 13-14). Its significance is constrained by validation on one frozen implementation and the absence of evidence that the audit transfers to materially different hybrid stacks or concurrent serving.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Excellent. The contract, target statuses, cohort-to-claim authorization, and denominator distinctions make a complex systems result unusually easy to audit (Tables 2, 8, and 9; Figure 3). Figures and tables are legible, the paper repeatedly prevents overinterpretation, and the appendices resolve important definitions. The density is high but does not materially impede evaluation.
dimension_justifications.soundness: The paper makes appropriately bounded claims and supplies unusually concrete within-stack evidence: the 96-cell factorial, storage witnesses, selected independent attention/GDN calculations, and live fault controls are clearly specified (Sections 4-5; Figure 3; Tables 6, 11, and 16). However, equality across ownership arms is principally a relational oracle, the independent numerical checks cover selected captured-input boundaries rather than end-to-end behavior, and dispatch provenance lacks a compiled-binary/autotuning identity (Section 6; Table 9, p. 17).

ethics_concerns: No specific unaddressed ethics violation is evident from the PDF. The paper includes an ethics statement and confines the work to systems behavior on PG-19 while acknowledging that efficiency can affect deployment scale (Appendix A, p. 15).
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to provide a closed source/environment identity or discovery that replay receipts cannot be tied to the reported execution.
Any mismatch in independently recomputed end-to-end outputs or storage predicates under the stated frozen setup.
Evidence that the observed savings or isolation properties disappear under minimally changed page, precision, scheduling, or hybrid-runtime conditions while claims remain general.
Fault experiments showing undetected ownership corruption or clean controls failing under matched execution.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A terminally closed, independently rebuildable artifact identity and clean-room validation of the primary replay.
Cross-stack results covering another hybrid model/runtime, compiled recurrent kernels, additional KV precision/page/length settings, and concurrent scheduling.
A candidate-independent end-to-end validation on a tractable subset together with broader preregistered operator coverage.
A comparative ablation demonstrating that the integrated audit detects or diagnoses failures beyond a well-defined conventional baseline.

issues.evidence_needed: A terminal manifest, reproducible environment lock, and an independent clean-room replay report.
issues.observed_evidence: The paper states that post-ledger pycache files broke terminal code-tree closure and that the derivative binds raw bytes and replay rather than a closed original-run identifier. Table 9 correspondingly notes that terminal recursive code-tree closure failed.
issues.required_fix: Release or describe a content-addressed terminal source tree and immutable environment/launcher image for the executed run, with an explicit mapping from that identity to the raw-artifact ledger and aggregate.
issues.verification_test: A clean-room evaluator should reconstruct the declared environment from the released identity, rerun the registered protocol, and verify the source/tree hashes plus all expected raw-byte and aggregate bindings.
issues.why_it_matters: This weakens the otherwise strong provenance story: replaying supplied artifacts is not equivalent to independently establishing that the reported GPU results arose from an immutable, complete source/environment snapshot.

issues.evidence_needed: Per-stack replayable receipts and a cross-stack summary of target coverage and limitations.
issues.location: Section 4.1-4.3, pp. 6-7; Table 7, p. 15; Appendix I, pp. 21-22
issues.observed_evidence: The primary evidence is one Qwen3.5 configuration on H20-3e hardware with BF16 KV, one page size, one partial-tail length, N<=32, eight PG-19 books, and sequential round-major execution on one CUDA stream. The paper explicitly excludes scheduler, concurrent-kernel, eviction, multi-document, and broad benchmark behavior.
issues.required_fix: Add preregistered transfer experiments spanning another hybrid model/runtime, a compiled recurrent path, multiple page/length/precision settings, and at least one concurrent or ragged-batch scheduling condition; retain the same claim-boundary discipline.
issues.verification_test: For each new stack, execute all applicable contract targets, include a failure-injection matrix, and report whether the audit detects faults without semantic regressions in matched clean controls.
issues.why_it_matters: The central audit idea may transfer, but the present evidence cannot establish that it remains practical or sufficient across different hybrid designs, optimized kernels, precision formats, scheduling policies, and lifecycle patterns where ownership bugs arise.

issues.evidence_needed: Candidate-independent end-to-end outputs or state sidecars, a preregistered sampling plan, and fault outcomes.
issues.location: Sections 5.4-5.6, pp. 10-11; Table 9, p. 17; Table 16, p. 21
issues.observed_evidence: Cross-cell and cross-N equality uses canonical digests of executions sharing much of the implementation. The attention oracle covers eight selected rows conditional on captured post-RoPE inputs, while the GDN oracle covers four post-normalization transitions and explicitly omits upstream normalization, projections, convolution, other layers, and end-to-end logits.
issues.required_fix: Add an independent end-to-end reference on a tractable subset, plus broader preregistered sampling of layers/tokens/lengths and faults that perturb upstream construction; distinguish exact checks from tolerance-based numerical checks.
issues.verification_test: Run the reference implementation on held-out documents and schedules, compare token trajectories/logits and state at declared boundaries, and show that injected upstream and ownership faults are rejected.
issues.why_it_matters: These checks substantially raise confidence in selected boundaries but cannot rule out common-mode or upstream errors that preserve equality across the four ownership arms. This is the main ceiling on a stronger soundness assessment.

issues.evidence_needed: A scoped comparative audit-coverage study with matched faults and baseline definitions.
issues.location: Section 2, pp. 3-4; Appendix G, Table 14, p. 20
issues.observed_evidence: The paper responsibly acknowledges that block sharing, COW, lifecycle testing, metamorphic relations, independent checking, and denominator separation are prior art. Its novelty is the integration, but the evaluation does not directly compare the integrated audit with a conventional test suite or ablate which receipts/fault gates add decision-relevant detection value.
issues.required_fix: Add an ablation or case-study comparison showing which realistic faults evade a baseline test strategy but are exposed by specific ForkAudit receipt classes or replay predicates.
issues.verification_test: Use a predeclared set of faults and report detection/diagnostic coverage for the baseline and progressively augmented audit, without converting targeted positive controls into a completeness claim.
issues.why_it_matters: Without such an ablation, readers cannot tell whether the full audit contract offers materially more practical assurance than a smaller set of existing testing and instrumentation practices.

llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was generated with LLM assistance from the frozen PDF and supplied rubric only; no source code, artifacts, prior reviews, or external evidence were inspected.
paper_summary: ForkAudit proposes an executable evidence contract for request isolation and memory accounting when a hybrid LLM forks continuations sharing token-indexed KV and recurrent GDN state. On a frozen Qwen3.5-35B-A3B/vLLM H20 configuration, it compares four KV-by-GDN ownership policies over 96 rank/fan-out/cell configurations, checks lifecycle storage predicates and registered semantic digests, evaluates selected independent attention and GDN operators, injects nine targeted live faults, and separates allocator outcomes from broader service-capacity claims. The paper also reports clearly separated deployment and cache-on/off context cohorts.
questions: Can the authors provide a terminally closed, independently rebuildable source/environment identity for the primary GPU run, given the explicit failure of recursive code-tree closure?

How does ForkAudit perform on at least one additional hybrid architecture and a compiled optimized recurrent implementation, with concurrent/ragged scheduling rather than sequential round-major execution?

Can the authors add a small end-to-end independent-reference experiment that validates upstream construction and all relevant hybrid transitions, not only selected post-capture attention and GDN boundaries?
What evidence shows that the integrated audit catches realistic failures not already exposed by a conventional ownership/unit-test suite plus existing metamorphic testing?
strengths: The paper distinguishes storage ownership, semantic equivalence, independent operator checks, fault sensitivity, and allocator denominators rather than treating any one as proof of the others (Sections 3-4 and 6).
The factorial design and Table 8 prevent inappropriate pooling of the primary audit, earlier capacity, lifecycle, deployment, and serving cohorts.

Limitations are unusually candid: sequential single-stream execution, selected rather than end-to-end oracles, one model/geometry, and lack of NVML or capacity evidence are all explicit (Section 6 and Appendix I).
The memory result is carefully interpreted: shared document KV lowers final allocated delta at N=32, whereas borrowed GDN changes allocation timing rather than final memory (Table 6, p. 11).
strongest_verified_contribution: Within the stated frozen stack, the strongest verified result is the phase-aware ownership audit: all four policies have matching registered outputs/state while storage receipts demonstrate post-transition disjoint mutable GDN state and private tail handling, with targeted faults reaching their predefined gates (Section 5.4-5.6; Figure 3; Tables 6 and 11).
